formal_statement: ¬ (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (α : Type) (S : Finset α) (roots labelled : Finset ℕ) (lab : ℕ → Finset α), PEqualNP.TopForm.IsAO2 n C → ∀ R : ℕ → ℕ → Prop, R = Relation.ReflTransGen (fun ra rb => ra < rb ∧ ∃ rj, rb = n + rj ∧ rj < C.gates.length ∧ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C rj).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧ ra ∈ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C rj).inputs) → (∀ m ∈ labelled, (m < n ∨ ∃ j, m = n + j ∧ j < C.gates.length ∧ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and) ∧ (lab m).card ≤ 2) → (∀ a ∈ S, ∃ r ∈ roots, ∃ m1 ∈ labelled, R m1 r ∧ a ∈ lab m1) → S.card ≤ roots.card + {jm : ℕ | jm < C.gates.length ∧ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C jm).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧ (∃ r2 ∈ roots, R (n + jm) r2) ∧ ({x3 : α | ∃ m3 ∈ labelled, R m3 ((PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C jm).inputs.getD 0 0) ∧ x3 ∈ lab m3}).Nonempty ∧ ({x4 : α | ∃ m4 ∈ labelled, R m4 ((PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C jm).inputs.getD 1 0) ∧ x4 ∈ lab m4}).Nonempty ∧ Disjoint {x5 : α | ∃ m5 ∈ labelled, R m5 ((PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C jm).inputs.getD 0 0) ∧ x5 ∈ lab m5} {x6 : α | ∃ m6 ∈ labelled, R m6 ((PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C jm).inputs.getD 1 0) ∧ x6 ∈ lab m6}}.ncard + {m7 : ℕ | m7 ∈ labelled ∧ (lab m7).card = 2}.ncard)
plain_statement: It is false that: Take an AND/OR circuit, each gate reading exactly two earlier wires. Some input or AND wires carry a label of at most two elements; the label set of a wire is the union of the labels of labelled wires with an OR-only path to it. If a finite set S lies in the union of the label sets of k roots, then |S| is at most k, plus the OR gates with an OR-only path to a root whose two inputs have nonempty disjoint label sets, plus the labelled wires with two labels.
title: It is false that: Glue lemma: covered labels are at most roots plus disjoint OR merges plus two-label wires (fan-in-two AND/OR circuits)
